# Synthetic matrix fixtures (E10d)

**These are not captures.** Each file is a copy of a real fixture in the folder above, with the fields below
changed, for the five states the real backend cannot be made to produce on demand (see the "States that cannot be
produced for real" section of `../README.md`). They were written on 2026-10-16 by one Python 3 standard-library
script run with `python -I` outside the repository, which loads the source file, changes exactly these fields and
writes compact JSON. Every text put in is copied from the backend code named beside it. Figures marked "made up"
were never measured; they exist only so the page has something of the right shape to show.

`contract.test.js` checks that each file has exactly the keys of its source, so a synthetic file cannot drift from
the real shape.

| File | Source | Changed fields |
|---|---|---|
| `run-checksum-mismatch.json` | `run-complete-100.json` | `gather[2].verified` false; `verification.blocksWithBadChecksum` 1, `mismatchedElements` 37 (made up), `parallelChecksum` 64 zeros (made up), `checksumsMatch` false, `passed` false; `timing.derived.speedup` and `computeBoundSpeedup` null, `speedupWithheldReason` `MatrixTexts.WITHHELD_MISMATCH`. `outcome` stays COMPLETE (`MatrixAssembly`: complete means no block missing). |
| `run-evicted-block.json` | `run-complete-100.json` | `computes[3]` (node 4) FAILED at CALL, `METHOD_THREW` with its `RemoteFailureKind` description, `failureClass` `MatrixComputeException`, `nodeReason` `INPUT_MISSING`, message and `nodeMessage` from `MatrixEndpointLogic.missing` (collective id from this run's scatter), `timeToFailureNanos` = its old round trip (made up), `roundTripNanos`, `computeNanos`, `checksum`, `replyLamport`, `lamportAfterReply` null; `gather[3]` NOT_ATTEMPTED "There is no block to fetch: its compute ended FAILED." with latency, bytes, `reportedChecksum`, `verified` and Lamport values null; `gather[4]` (node 5) FAILED at CALL, `METHOD_THREW`, `MatrixComputeException` with the `BLOCK_MISSING` message of `MatrixEndpointLogic` (a fetch row has no `nodeReason` field), `timeToFailureNanos` = its old latency (made up), `latencyNanos`, `replyBytes`, `verified`, `replyLamport`, `lamportAfterReply` null; `outcome` PARTIAL; `verification.rowsReceived` 60, `blocksMissing` 2, `elementsCompared` 6000, `parallelChecksum`, `checksumsMatch`, `passed` null; speedups null with the PARTIAL withheld reason (copied from `run-partial.json`). |
| `run-timeouts.json` | `run-complete-100.json` | `computes[1]` (node 2) the node's own timeout: FAILED at CALL, `METHOD_THREW`, `MatrixComputeException`, `nodeReason` `COMPUTE_TIMED_OUT`, message from `NodeExecutor` with the capture's `computeTimeoutMillis`, `timeToFailureNanos` 2004512300 (made up); `computes[2]` (node 3) the root's wait bound: FAILED at CALL, `TIMED_OUT` with its description, no exception or cause class, `nodeReason` and `nodeMessage` null, message from `ParallelMatrixExecutor.abandonedCompute` (12000 ms = the capture's `computeWaitMillis`), every Lamport value null, `timeToFailureNanos` 12000873100 (made up); `gather[1]` and `gather[2]` NOT_ATTEMPTED as above; `timing.measured.computePhaseNanos` 12001250400 (made up) and `parallelTotalNanos` raised by the same amount; `otherNanos` and `communicationShare` recomputed from those; `outcome` PARTIAL with the verification and speedup changes as above. |

(`ParallelMatrixExecutor.deadlineReason`), `roundTripNanos`, `computeNanos`, `checksum` and Lamport values null; `gather[4]` NOT_ATTEMPTED "There is no block to fetch: its compute ended NOT_ATTEMPTED."; `gather[3]` NOT_ATTEMPTED "The run's deadline of 10000 ms had passed before this fetch."; `outcome` PARTIAL with the verification and speedup changes as above. |
